His team also reported that he is considering backing another candidate or party, or remaining outside electoral politics while he works in the private sector.

Zelensky Informs UN Secretary-General Guterres About Russian Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky, following Russia’s massive strike on a shopping mall in his hometown of Kryvy Rih, said he spoke with UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday, Aug. 21. The two discussed Russia’s continued attacks on Ukraine, civilian casualties, and global food security threats.

EU Pledges Support for Ukraine’s Anti-Graft Efforts Amid New ‘Forrest Gump’ Probe — EU ambassadors met the heads of Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO), in Kyiv on Friday, Aug. 21, pledging continued support for the country’s reform efforts. The meeting comes two days after a new corruption probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” targeted Sense Bank.

8,500 North Korean Troops Now in Russia, Ukraine Says — North Korea has sent a new contingent of around 8,500 troops to Russia, including approximately 400 drone operators, Ukrainian military intelligence Deputy Head Vadym Skibitskyi told CNN. The troops are expected to reinforce Russian rear positions, potentially freeing Russian forces for frontline assaults. Skibitskyi said Moscow could seek up to 50,000 additional North Korean troops, while Pyongyang is also supplying ballistic missiles and

Russia’s Shopping Mall Strike on Zelensky’s Hometown Kills 15, Injures 130 as Rescue Continues — Russia struck a shopping mall in central Ukraine’s Kryvyi Rih on Friday afternoon, killing at least 15 and injuring over 130. Officials said casualties are likely to rise as they warned of additional strikes as jet-powered drones continue circling around the city at low altitudes.

Wartime Government in Ukraine and the Zelensky-Fedorov Clash — The dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and a series of corruption allegations involving figures close to Bankova have sharpened questions about whether Ukraine’s wartime centralization remains subject to meaningful constitutional checks. While martial law and postponed elections are legal, the deeper issue is whether parliament, oversight bodies and other institutions retain the power to hold the presidency accountable.

Ukrainian Authorities Detain Chornomorsk Port Official in Bribery Probe — Ukrainian authorities detained a Chornomorsk port official and an alleged intermediary over a Hr. 500,000 ($11,200) payment demanded from a contractor working on railway infrastructure at the port.

Russia Seeks New Charges Against Teenager Accused of Blowing Up FSB Building in Minecraft — Russia is seeking new charges against Nikita Uvarov, a teenager arrested in 2020 for putting up political leaflets who was subsequently accused of blowing up an FSB building in-game in preparation for real-world scenarios. The new charges were brought to him a month before he was scheduled to be released earlier this year.

NATO Military Committee to Return to Ukraine After Eight Years — Ukraine will host the NATO Military Committee in October, marking the first such visit in eight years, Ukrainian Armed Forces Commander Mykhailo Drapatyi said. Drapatyi discussed the frontline situation and Ukraine’s priorities with NATO Military Committee Chair Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, including long-range strikes, infantry tactics, battlefield robotics and air defense.

More Than 15 Explosions in 20 Minutes Rock Occupied Crimea Amid Power Outages — More than 15 explosions were reported near Simferopol amid alleged drone activity, including sightings near the Tavriyska Thermal Power Plant. Russian authorities claimed that two people were killed and six injured, while Russian-controlled utilities reported damage to energy infrastructure and power outages across the occupied peninsula.

Trump Rejects Push to Give Ukraine Starlink for Long-Range Strikes on Russia – FT — President Donald Trump has rejected Ukraine’s request to persuade Elon Musk to allow Starlink for drone strikes inside Russia, the Financial Times reported. Kyiv says the satellite network could help target Russian ballistic missile launchers more precisely as Ukraine faces dwindling Patriot interceptor stocks ahead of winter.

Suspected Russian Handguns Found Near Berlin: German Media — German security services have uncovered two handguns hidden near Berlin that they suspect were intended for Russian agents preparing “kinetic operations,” German media reported. The discovery comes amid growing concerns over Russian sabotage and assassination plots targeting Germany’s defense industry and Ukraine supporters.

Russian Social Network VK Sues Apple Over App Store Removal — VK, Russia’s largest social media conglomerate, said it has filed a lawsuit against Apple over the tech giant’s delisting of its applications in June. VK is now seeking 58 million rubles per day in damages, which include 50 million rubles for the VK platform, 3 million for the Odnolassniki network, and 5 million for the VK Music service.

Nord Stream Suspect Arrested on Set of Film About the Sabotage — A Ukrainian diver suspected by German prosecutors of helping sabotage the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022 was arrested in Pula, Croatia, while reportedly working as a consultant on a Hollywood film dramatizing the attack. The film, Snake Island, is directed by Doug Liman and stars Sean Penn and Adrien Brody. German prosecutors accuse the suspect of belonging to a group that planted explosives on the pipelines near Denmark.

Ukraine Sanctions Russia’s Hit ‘Masha and the Bear’ Cartoon — Ukraine has sanctioned the producers and distributors of the popular Russian children’s cartoon “Masha and the Bear,” paving the way for its content to be blocked and monetization restricted. Kyiv says the series is a Kremlin propaganda tool with no place on Ukrainian children’s screens.

Australia Hits Russian Man With ‘Foreign Interference’ Charges Over Plot to Infiltrate Ukrainian Military — Australia said it arrested a 27-year-old dual Australian-Russian national on “foreign interference” charges. The man is said to have received “military-style” training in Russia in 2024 before joining the Ukrainian military in March 2025 in an attempt to pass on intelligence to Russian security services.

Ukraine Planned 1,000-Drone Swarm to Paralyze Moscow Airports — Ukraine reportedly planned to unleash up to 1,000 autonomous AI-powered drones on Moscow’s airports in a single night, aiming to overwhelm air defenses, cripple flights and pressure the Kremlin back to negotiations. The operation was halted after former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov’s July departure.

Russia Deploys North Korean Ballistic Missiles Within Reach of 7 Ukrainian Regions — Russia is preparing to expand its use of North Korean ballistic missiles, with six launchers reportedly deployed in Voronezh Oblast, the ISW said. Ukrainian military intelligence said North Korea had transferred around 50 KN-23, KN-24 and upgraded KN-30 missiles to Russia by July. From Voronezh, the missiles could reach the Sumy, Kharkiv, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions.

Russia Strikes Ukraine-Moldova Border Crossing for Second Night in a Row — Russia attacked a Ukrainian border crossing with Moldova for the second night in a row, damaging infrastructure and forcing the checkpoint to close, Kyiv said. The strikes come after Moldova reported a drone entering its airspace.

‘Don’t Even Think About It’: Ex-Danish FM Warns Russia Amid NATO Drills — NATO’s Nordic allies are strengthening military readiness and air defenses as tensions with Russia persist. Former Danish Foreign Minister Jeppe Kofod urged faster defense spending, closer regional cooperation and stronger protection of critical infrastructure. He said NATO exercises near Kaliningrad demonstrate readiness to respond, while stressing continued military and air-defense support for Ukraine.

Mariupol Volunteer Safe After Risking Everything to Save Son Allegedly Threatened by Russia’s FSB — Ukrainian volunteer Mykhailo Puryshev says he is safe after traveling to Moscow to save his 18-year-old son, whom he says Russia’s FSB threatened with death or being sent to fight against Ukraine if he refused to cooperate. Puryshev has not disclosed how he escaped Russia.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Major Lukoil Refinery, Military Airfield as Russia Claims 325 UAVs Downed — Ukraine struck the Perm oil refinery and Marynovka military airfield in separate long-range attacks, Zelensky said. He also reported earlier damage to a Russian Su-34 and a facility used to prepare and launch attack drones.

Russia Unleashes 135 Drones on Ukraine, Killing 2 in Kharkiv Region and Injuring 6 in Sumy — Russia launched 135 drones at Ukraine overnight, with 107 intercepted or suppressed. Strikes damaged homes and civilian infrastructure in Sumy, where 6 were injured, while two women were killed and two people wounded in Kharkiv region.

Ex-Defense Minister Fedorov Plans US Trip for Defense Tech, Team Denies Political Meetings — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is planning a US trip focused on defense technology projects, his team says, pushing back on reports linking the visit to political outreach.

How Energy-Exporting Russia Is Turning Into a Fuel Importer – Thanks to Ukraine — Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed Russia has begun importing fuel as Ukrainian strikes disrupt refineries, squeeze gasoline supplies and force rationing.

Romania Destroys Explosive Marine Drone Near Major Black Sea Gas Project — Romania destroyed an explosive-carrying marine drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project after it approached critical infrastructure in the Black Sea. Kyiv told Bucharest the vessel was not Ukrainian, while Romania’s president blamed Russia.

Zelensky: Ukraine Downed 90% of Russian Cruise Missiles, Vows Long-Range Response — Ukraine intercepted about 90% of Russian cruise missiles in the overnight attack, but Zelensky said ballistic missiles remain far harder to stop and urged partners to provide more Patriot interceptors. He also pledged additional resources for Ukraine’s long-range strike capabilities.

Finland suspects Russian plane of violating its airspace — Finland’s Defense Ministry said it is investigating a suspected Russian aircraft incursion into its airspace, following similar incidents involving Russian military aircraft in May and June.

Russia Places German Journalist Michael Martens on Wanted List — Russia placed Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) correspondent Michael Martens on its Interior Ministry wanted list on Aug. 15, following his question to President Volodymyr Zelensky about increasing Russian military casualties during his meeting with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić on Aug. 8.

Koretskyi Orders Sale of Sense Bank, Pledges Sale Revenue to Ukraine’s Defense Forces — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said the Ministry of Finance has been given a task to accelerate the sale of Sense Bank through a transparent and competitive process, after anti-graft agencies announced a new probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” and searched the bank’s premises on Wednesday, Aug. 19. Revenue from the sale will be directed to the country’s Defense Forces.

Russian Missile Strike Partially Halts Arcelor Mittal Kryvyi Rih Operations, Kills 2 Workers — A Russian missile strike on ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih killed two workers and injured 13 others overnight on Aug. 16. The attack damaged key energy and blast furnace units, forcing Ukraine's largest steelmaker to partially halt production.

Russia’s Greatest Enemy Is Inside the Kremlin — Staying loyal to Vladimir Putin has become a fatal mistake for generals, oligarchs, and inner circle officials who thought obedience guaranteed safety. Autocratic regimes rot from the inside long before they shatter publicly, and Moscow is now witnessing unprecedented purges as liquid financial reserves drain at a record speed. Loyalty no longer buys wealth or protection in modern Russia, leaving top commanders and technocrats caught in a trap wher

Russian Strikes Injure 2 in Dnipropetrovsk, Set Private Home in Pavlohrad Ablaze — Russian forces launched nearly 50 drone and artillery attacks across three districts of Dnipropetrovsk region on Thursday, Aug. 20, injuring two men and damaging civilian infrastructure. A separate attack on Pavlohrad set a private home ablaze.

Fedorov Brings the Wartime Election Debate into the Open — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov’s call for wartime elections has transformed him from a dismissed Zelensky ally into a potential rival. Dmytro Kuleba’s parallel argument shows the debate is broader than one man, while Valery Zaluzhny remains the strongest potential challenger to the president.

Dniester Reservoir Water Level Hits Record Low — The Dniester Reservoir has reached its lowest record marked on Thursday, Aug. 20, after natural inflow fell to about one-fifth of the seasonal norm. Ukrhydroenergo said it is prioritizing drinking water and local communities over hydropower generation.

Death Toll in Russia’s Attack on Kyiv Rises to 17, 42 People Wounded — Russian forces launched a major drone and missile barrage on Kyiv overnight into Thursday, Aug. 20, killing at least 16 people and injuring at least 39, as strikes damaged residential buildings, a children’s hospital, a school, and other civilian infrastructure. Latest strikes on Holosiivskyi district left two people dead and three others injured.

Putin Expects Ukraine to Break This Winter, First Deputy Head of Presidential Office Kyslytsya Says — Serhii Kyslytsya, first deputy head of Ukraine’s Presidential Office, said Thursday, Aug. 20, that Russian President Vladimir Putin has little interest in negotiations and may be even less willing to talk through winter. His remarks come as Kyiv is working to prepare its defenses, critical infrastructure, and residents for the upcoming winter.

Ukrainian Man Arrested in Poland Over Alleged Russian-Backed Plot — Poland’s Internal Security Agency arrested a 63-year-old Ukrainian citizen in Warsaw over an alleged attempt to assassinate a representative of Ukraine’s defense industry in Irpin. Polish authorities say Serhii P. allegedly planted an improvised explosive device under the victim’s car on behalf of Russian intelligence services before fleeing to Warsaw.

Ukrainian Speaking Club to Mark Independence Day With Free Online Session — Language Lab is hosting a free online Speaking Club on Aug. 23 to mark Ukraine's Independence Day, a holiday that carries added weight this year as the country marks 35 years since declaring independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. Open to all skill levels, the Zoom session blends Ukrainian-English conversation practice with reflections on national identity, connecting learners worldwide with native-speaking facilitat

‘Every Third Building’: Klitschko on Russia’s Damage to Kyiv — Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian attacks have caused varying degrees of damage to around 4,000 of Kyiv’s 12,000 buildings. He said each Russian attack costs the city budget approximately Hr.500 million. Kyiv is also continuing to expand shelters and prepare its energy infrastructure for the winter.

NBU Will Interview Sense Bank Chief, Opens Board-Wide Suitability Probe — NBU will interview Sense Bank chief Oleksiy Stupak on Aug. 26 over his professional fitness and has opened a separate probe into the collective suitability of the bank's entire supervisory board. Governor Andriy Pyshny cited a hidden management structure predating the bank's 2023 nationalization, capping a week that saw the Cabinet remove the board's chairman amid a NABU bail-laundering probe.

‘Ukraine Must Decide’: EU on Possible Wartime Elections — The European Commission said Ukraine should decide when to hold elections based on its Constitution and legal framework, while meeting democratic standards. EU spokesperson Anitta Hipper said the bloc was ready to support Ukraine throughout the electoral process if Kyiv decides to hold a vote.

Putin Avoids Sochi for Record 322 Days Amid Drone Threat — Russian President Vladimir Putin has gone 322 days without a public visit to Sochi, according to the Russian independent outlet Agentstvo. Putin previously visited the resort city at least twice (but, up to over two dozen times) a year, but skipped his usual spring trip in 2026. The outlet linked the change to increased Ukrainian drone activity and reported that visits to Sochi by other Russians have also declined.

Romanian F-16 Destroys Explosives-Laden Marine Drone Near Black Sea Gas Project — A Romanian F-16 fighter destroyed an explosives-laden marine drone near the strategic Neptun Deep gas project on Thursday, as Bucharest blamed Russia for the incident. The attack comes amid growing drone activity along NATO’s eastern flank and renewed Russian aerial assaults on Ukraine.

Ukraine Calls for Urgent Global Response After Russia’s 9-Hour Assault — Ukraine’s FM urged allies to provide more air-defense interceptors, tighten sanctions, and help develop anti-ballistic defenses after Russia’s nearly nine-hour attack. The barrage killed at least 14 people, damaged civilian infrastructure, and left 13,000 Odesa residents without power.

Ukraine Gains Ground Near Kharkiv, Foils Russian Flag-Raising Attempt — Ukrainian forces recently advanced in the Kharkiv Oblast, while Russian forces reportedly made limited gains near Kupyansk, the Institute for the Study of War reported on Wednesday. Ukrainian forces also thwarted a Russian flag-raising attempt near Vovchansk and continued strikes against Russian military assets and logistics in the occupied Luhansk Oblast.

Portrait of the Ukrainian Nation at 35 Years of Restored Independence — Over 35 years, Ukraine has overcome key regional divisions, transformed its attitude toward Russia and moved closer to Europe in terms of values. At the same time, the prolonged war is exhausting society. Despite this, the majority remains ready to resist.

Will Fedorov Meet Trump in the US? | Bohdan Nahaylo — TVP World’s Sascha Fahrbach and Kyiv Post’s Chief Editor, Bohdan Nahaylo, discuss Russia’s latest attacks on Kyiv, the state of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, growing political tensions in the capital, the corruption probe surrounding senior officials, and Mykhailo Fedorov’s increasingly prominent political role.

Ukraine Strikes Major Oil Refinery in Tatarstan as Drone Barrage Hits Russia — Ukraine struck the TANЕCO oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, with Ukrainian-made FP-1 drones, according to defense company Fire Point. Russian monitoring channels reported at least 12 deaths. The overnight barrage also targeted an oil terminal and power substation, further hitting Russia’s critical energy infrastructure.

Russia Targets Ukraine-Moldova Border Checkpoint as Moscow Unleashes a Multi-Layered Attack — Russia launched a massive overnight attack involving ballistic and cruise missiles and 168 Shahed-type drones. Ukraine’s Air Force said it intercepted most cruise missiles and drones, while Zelensky called for more Patriot interceptors amid deadly strikes across several regions.

Ukraine May Have Left 2 Russian Frigates Unable to Launch Missiles After Novorossiysk Strike — Satellite imagery reportedly shows serious damage to Russia’s Admiral Makarov and Admiral Essen after Ukraine’s Aug. 12 strike on Novorossiysk. Russian and Ukrainian OSINT sources claim both frigates suffered damage to their missile-launch and combat-control systems, though the extent remains unconfirmed.

Fedorov vs Zelensky? Ukraine Entering a New Political Season? — The Verkhovna Rada has appointed a defense minister, and, as expected, Mykhailo Fedorov was not returned to the post. He has recorded a video address criticizing the current system and, conroversially, calling for elections.

‘People, Not Robots’: Ukraine’s Soldiers Justify Human Role Amid Drone Revolution — Drones now destroy about 90% of targets in Ukraine, making traditional airborne assaults increasingly impractical. Yet newly trained paratroopers say demanding physical and psychological training remains vital because technology cannot replace the soldiers who ultimately hold territory.

Ukraine: A Dismissed Innovative Defense Minister Calls for Elections — Fedorov has called for a secure way to hold elections during the war, warning democracy cannot depend on Russia. Critics see the move as a potential campaign launch and warn political turmoil could threaten Ukraine’s defense capabilities.

Hungary Drops Money Laundering Case Against Oschadbank Cash Convoy — Hungary's National Tax and Customs Administration has closed its money laundering case against Oschadbank's cash convoy, finding the seized banknotes and gold originated from a legitimate interbank deal with Raiffeisen Bank International. Lawyer Lóránt Horváth said the closure undercuts Budapest's original justification for the March seizure and detention of seven Ukrainian couriers.

At Least 6 Kyiv Markets Damaged or Destroyed in Russian Attacks Since 2022 — Ten days after a Russian strike devastated Kyiv’s Pochaina flea market, vendors are selling salvaged goods on the street as they struggle to rebuild their livelihoods.

Zelensky Tasks New Defense Minister Khmara With Expanding Ukraine’s Deep Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky has tasked newly appointed Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara with expanding long-range strikes, boosting air defense and reforming defense procurement and frontline supply.

Zelensky Names 29-Year-Old Former Schoolteacher Hero of Ukraine After Drone-Zone Rescue — Former teacher Vladyslav Polskyi, now an assault company commander, received Ukraine’s highest honor after personally evacuating two wounded soldiers under Russian drone threat.

Massive Russian Missile and Drone Attack on Kyiv Kills 15, Injures 39, Hits Hospital, School and Homes — Russia hit Kyiv with ballistic and Kalibr missiles and jet-powered drones, killing 15 and injuring 39 as homes, a hospital and school were damaged.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Ukraine Repels 189 Combat Clashes as Pokrovsk Axis Sees Heaviest Fighting During 24-Hour Period — The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) repelled 189 combat clashes nationwide over the past 24 hours, with the heaviest fighting concentrated on the Pokrovsk axis, where Russian forces launched 26 assaults. The General Staff reported at least 33 Russian troops killed and 15 wounded in that sector alone.

Ukraine’s Government Removes Sense Bank Chairman Amid Anti-Corruption Probe — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced Wednesday, Aug. 19, that the government removed the chairman of state-owned Sense Bank’s supervisory board, seeking to oust its CEO next. The decision follows a NABU investigation that claimed bank officials helped launder HR. 150 million (roughly $3.3 million) to post bail for a suspect in an earlier corruption case.

Ukraine's Ex-Defense Chief Makes Risky Bet by Entering Electoral Politics — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov delivered a video address on Tuesday, Aug. 18, that called for wartime elections. Even his own supporters distanced themselves from the move, calling it a risky departure from his role as a reformer.

Stray Drone Crashes Into Turkish Police Station in Black Sea Port City Trabzon — A suspected drone crashed into the yard of a police station in Turkey’s Black Sea port city of Trabzon on Tuesday, Aug. 18, damaging four vehicles and shattering windows. No one was injured, but the authorities have launched an investigation into the aircraft’s origin.

Sense Bank Confirms Investigative Actions Following Corruption Probe — Sense Bank confirmed Wednesday, Aug. 19, that law enforcement conducted investigative actions tied to the “Forrest Gump” probe at its head office, investigating a HR. 150 million ($3.3 million) money-laundering scheme. According to anti-corruption officials, the funds were used to post bail for a suspect in the previous probe dubbed “Midas.”

Former Deputy Office Head Iryna Mudra Detained Overnight in Corruption Probe — Iryna Mudra, former deputy head of Ukraine’s Presidential Office, was detained on Wednesday, Aug. 19, and is currently undergoing investigative actions at the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU). According to Member of Parliament Oleksiy Honcharenko, Mudra will spend the night in a temporary detention facility.

Russian ‘Banderol’ Type Drone Strikes Zhytomyr Police Building, Kills 3, Injures 53 — A Russian “Banderol”-type drone struck Zhytomyr’s regional police headquarters on Wednesday, Aug. 19, killing 3 and injuring at least 53 people. National Police chief Maksym Tsutskiridze called the strike deliberate terror against those who protect civilians.

Putin Says Russian Economy Remains Stable Despite Attacks — Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia’s economic performance remained positive despite what he described as “terrorist” attacks on infrastructure. Speaking at a meeting on strategic development and national projects on Wednesday, Aug. 19, Putin said damaged logistics and storage facilities required reconstruction and called for measures to support financially strained regions.

Cultural Sovereignty and Agency: Ukraine’s 35-Year Journey to Reclaim Its Voice — For centuries, Russia sought to subsume Ukrainian identity into its own imperial narrative. Since 1991, Ukraine has steadily reclaimed its cultural voice. Russia’s full-scale war accelerated that process, demonstrating that culture is not decoration but a pillar of national security, sovereignty, and international agency.

Zelensky Sacks Deputy Office Head Iryna Mudra After NABU’s New ‘Forrest Gump’ Probe — Zelensky dismissed Iryna Mudra, the deputy head of the Presidential Office tasked with judicial reforms, shortly after the anti-graft agencies announced a new probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” targeting top officials, with Mudra among those reportedly implicated.

On Fedorov, Zelensky, Elections, and the Political Crisis — The first missed elections were for the Verkhovna Rada. And the first post-war elections should also be for the legislature, so that we can exit the war calmly, ensure a smooth transition of power, create a competitive environment primarily for the governing institution of peacetime, and form a government based on programs of action rather than rearranging chairs in offices.

Ukraine – What Is Fedorov Thinking? — Elections will likely just accentuate divisions in Ukrainian society – to be exploited by Putin, which is why Putin is pushing for them. And even Fedorov raising the issue now will signal division.

Russians Lured Into War With Wildberries, Ozon Warehouse Security Jobs — Russian job seekers are reportedly being lured into military service through fake warehouse security vacancies. Verstka found around 2,000 ads offering to guard Wildberries and Ozon facilities, with recruiters promising civilian work while actually proposing one-year defense ministry contracts.

Ukraine Arrests 2 Middle Eastern Men for Sabotaging Substation in Chernivtsi — The SBU said it arrested two men from an unspecified Middle Eastern country in western Ukraine’s Chernivtsi for setting a substation ablaze under the instructions of Russian intelligence. The episode marked a rare occurrence in which foreign nationals are named in similar schemes, though it is not without precedent.

Second Ukrainian Suspect in Nord Stream Case Arrested in Croatia — On Wednesday, German prosecutors said that Ukrainian national Vladimir Z. had been arrested in Pula, Croatia, over his alleged role in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions. Prosecutors accuse him of being part of a group led by former Ukrainian army officer Serhii K. that allegedly planted explosives on Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 near Denmark.

Ukraine Emerges From the Shadows of History as a Shaper of the New World Order — After centuries of struggle, Ukraine is moving from an object of others’ history toward becoming one of the architects creating a new global security order.

Verkhovna Rada Approves Sybiha as Foreign Minister With 266 Votes — Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada on Wednesday, Aug. 19, approved Andriy Sybiha as foreign minister, with 266 lawmakers voting in favor. Sybiha continued leading the Foreign Ministry during the government reshuffle but had temporarily served as acting minister before President Volodymyr Zelensky formally submitted his candidacy to the Ukrainian legislature, the Verkhovna Rada. The ministry said its priorities include strengthening intern

Iran Eyes US Military Targets in Europe if War Escalates — Iranian forces have considered striking US military targets in southeastern Europe and Cyprus if President Donald Trump escalates the war, according to people close to the Iranian regime cited by the Financial Times. Tehran has also examined attacks on subsea fiber-optic cables in the Strait of Hormuz and warned that any renewed US offensive could trigger retaliation beyond the Middle East.

Ukraine Says Russian ‘Safari’ Attack on Minibus Kills Four — A Russian drone strike on a minibus in frontline Kherson killed four civilians and wounded five others Wednesday, Ukrainian officials said. Kyiv accused Russian forces of conducting a “safari”-style hunt targeting civilians in the southern city, which faces frequent drone attacks from Russian positions across the Dnipro River.

BlueBird Tech Unveils Bebradrone-M UAV for Training Ukraine’s Interceptor Drone Operators — Ukraine’s BlueBird Tech has unveiled the Bebradrone-M, a fixed-wing UAV designed to train pilots and interceptor drone operators using real aerial targets. The drone can simulate reconnaissance aircraft and decoys, allowing teams to practice detection, pursuit and interception in scenarios designed to replicate battlefield conditions.

Ukraine Picks General to Run Defense Ministry as Civilian Status Rule Sparks Questions — Ukraine’s parliament appointed Maj. Gen. Yevhen Khmara as defense minister with 312 votes, following weeks of protests over Fedorov’s dismissal. Khmara’s appointment also faced a legal hurdle because Ukrainian law requires the defense minister to be a civilian.

Ukraine, Russia Swap 103 Prisoners Each in Latest Exchange — Ukraine and Russia exchanged 103 prisoners each on Aug. 19, bringing 103 Ukrainian soldiers home from Russian captivity. The released Ukrainians include troops from the Armed Forces, Border Guard Service, and National Guard who fought in Mariupol and across several regions.

Moscow Gas Stations Impose Fuel Limits as Russian Shortage Deepens — Moscow gas stations are rationing gasoline and diesel as a widening fuel shortage puts pressure on Russia’s capital, while authorities scramble to redirect supplies from other regions.

Trump Scales Back Joint Drills With South Korea — Trump’s decision to scale back US-South Korea military exercises has raised concerns about the consequences for regional security. Critics argue he overestimates his relationship with Kim Jong-un, potentially strengthening North Korea’s regime and aggression. Germany’s Süddeutsche Zeitung warns that the move could weaken Seoul’s trust in Washington and push South Korea toward new alliances.

NABU Starts ‘Forrest Gump’ Operation, Uncovers Crisis Plan — Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office are conducting a special operation targeting an alleged criminal organization led by a current and former lawmaker. During searches, investigators found a document outlining a crisis communication plan related to a Verkhovna Rada temporary investigative commission.

Open the Black Sea for Shipping! — The Russo-Ukrainian War is heating up in the Black Sea this summer, with tit-for-tat attacks on shipping. The Ukrainian economy is at risk and needs the help of Europeans, particularly the Baltic states.

Ukraine Needs Allies, Not Amnesia: Viktor Yushchenko in Azerbaijan — Former President Viktor Yushchenko’s visit to Azerbaijan drew criticism over his warm relationship with Ilham Aliyev. The controversy highlights a broader tension between Kyiv’s need for strategic partners and the democratic principles associated with the Orange Revolution and Maidan.

NATO Draws Up 3-Step Plan to Fight Russia if Putin Attacks the Baltics — NATO has reportedly developed a three-part strategy for a potential Russian attack on the Baltic states. According to Bild, the plan includes suppressing Russian missile systems, deploying autonomous drones along NATO’s borders and striking key military and logistical targets inside Russia.

EXPLAINER: 35 Years Ago Today, the World Held Its Breath — On this day in 1991, a failed hardline coup in Moscow became the final shock that pushed Ukraine from asserted sovereignty to independence. As Soviet authority faltered, Ukraine’s democratic forces, sovereignty Communists led by Leonid Kravchuk, and public protests in Kyiv, converged against a crumbling empire. Within days, the coup’s collapse cleared the way for parliament to meet on Aug. 24 and declare an independent Ukrainian state.

‘Zero Tolerance’: Polish Woman Charged After Alleged Nationality-Based Attack on Ukrainian Siblings — A 46-year-old Polish woman has been charged after allegedly verbally and physically attacking two Ukrainian siblings, aged 14 and 12, in Bydgoszcz. Police say the incident involved nationality-based insults and damage to the children’s toy drone.

Major Explosives Plant Hit Again as Ukrainian Drones Strike Across Russia Overnight — Ukrainian drones targeted the Sverdlov explosives plant in Dzerzhinsk, according to Russian and OSINT reports, marking another attack on the facility this year. Overnight strikes were also reported in Ufa, the Tula region, and near Moscow, with casualties reported in Ufa.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 18, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 18, 2026

Estonia Probes Possible Russian Sabotage After Fire at Defense Firm Supplying Ukraine — Estonia is investigating whether Russia was behind a suspected arson attack on Milrem Robotics, whose unmanned military systems are used in Ukraine.

2 Killed, 10 Wounded as Russia Hits Zaporizhzhia Region 1,019 Times in 24 Hours — Russian forces carried out 1,019 attacks across 52 settlements in the Zaporizhzhia region, including 717 drone strikes, 19 airstrikes and 276 artillery attacks. Two people were killed and 10 wounded.

Lavrov Threatens UK With ‘Consequences’ Over Ukraine War — Sergei Lavrov says Moscow could treat British involvement in Ukrainian strikes on Russia as participation in the war, escalating an earlier embassy warning to London.
